situation.summary: Tenant Iris Vale reported on 6 May 2025 that the shower and hot water were not working and the boiler had no power (S:initial-request, E001, E003). Northbridge categorised it as Electrical and offered the landlord the choice of his own contractor or an agency one. Ravi Sethi chose his own plumber and booked no agency contractor (E007, E010, E015). On 15 May Ravi said the plumber attended on 14 May and fixed it, based on a text from the plumber; no work description, report, invoice or boiler or electrical check details were provided (E018). The tenant has not confirmed the fix: her last recorded statement was still no hot water (E017, 13 May), her 15 May email asking for confirmation has no reply, and a voicemail was left (E019, E020). The request is still open at the decision moment and the letterbox issue she raised on 13 May has no recorded follow-up.
situation.task: Verify with tenant Iris Vale whether hot water and boiler power are now working, since the landlord's reported fix is unconfirmed and the tenant's last report said it was not.
situation.stageLabel: Landlord reports the repair is done; tenant has not confirmed; no written repair record; request open
situation.whoseMove: Northbridge is waiting on the tenant's confirmation, and the agency's move is next. Recommended next action: tenant.chase to Iris Vale by phone call, with a follow-up SMS if she does not answer, asking whether there is hot water at the taps and shower and whether the boiler has power. Reply-by: Monday 19 May 2025, 12:00 UTC (16 May is a Friday). Draft text: "Hi Iris, the landlord says his plumber fixed the hot water on 14 May. Can you tell us by Monday 19 May whether you now have hot water at the taps and in the shower, and whether the boiler has power? If it is still not working, or the boiler trips or sparks again, switch the boiler off at its isolator and tell us straight away. If anyone in the household would like an interpreter, tell us. Please also let us know the details of the letterbox problem you mentioned so we can log it." The landlord is not waiting on us now. Once the tenant replies, ask Ravi in writing for the plumber's work description, invoice and any electrical checks. Do not close the case or tell the landlord it is resolved until the tenant confirms.

decision.actionLabel: Chase the tenant by SMS to confirm whether hot water and boiler power are back after the landlord's plumber's visit, and ask for details of the letterbox fault
decision.message: Hi Iris, this is Maya Chen from Northbridge Lettings about your hot water at 17 Wrenfold Quay. Your landlord has told us his plumber came on 14 May and fixed the problem. We have not heard from you since, so please can you confirm by Monday 19 May whether: 1) you now have hot water at the taps and in the shower, and 2) the boiler now has power. If it is still not working, reply and we will take it straight back to your landlord. If the boiler shows any sign of burning, sparking or tripping, stop using it and tell us straight away. On the letterbox you mentioned on 13 May: please reply with a short description of what is wrong (a photo would help) and we will log it as a separate repair. If it is easier to speak, call us. Thank you, Maya
decision.rationale: This is a landlord-managed repair. The landlord says his plumber fixed it on 14 May, but he only has the plumber's text to go on (E018). The tenant's last report, on 13 May, was still no hot water (E017), and she has not confirmed anything since. The voicemail (E019) and email (E020) on 15 May got no reply. We cannot close the job or tell the landlord it is settled without her confirmation. The agency treated loss of hot water as urgent (E004), and it is Friday afternoon. Waiting until Monday without trying a different channel could leave a household with no hot water over the weekend without us knowing. So we chase now by SMS, a different channel from the voicemail and email, and set a reply-by date of Monday. The letterbox question (E017) is new, not a repeat of an earlier ask. Maya promised to follow it up and nothing has been done, so we ask for the details in the same message and log it as a separate request. The landlord is not waiting on us. He asked to be told only if the problem persists (E018), so no landlord message goes out this turn.
decision.expectedOutcome: The tenant replies to say either that hot water and boiler power are back, which supports closing the job once the landlord's position on paperwork is noted, or that the fault continues, which goes straight back to the landlord. She may also describe the letterbox fault so it can be logged as a separate request.

decision.message:

1) Do you now have hot water at the taps and in the shower?
2) Does the boiler have power and stay on?
If it is still not working, or stops working again, please tell us straight away and we will take it back to your landlord the same day. If you notice a burning smell, sparking or anything else that seems unsafe at the boiler, stop using it and contact us immediately.
On the letterbox you mentioned on 13 May: please tell us what is wrong with it (a photo helps) and we will log it as a separate request.
If anyone at home would find it easier to speak in another language, please let us know. Thank you, Maya
decision.rationale: The job is landlord-managed (E007, E010, E015). The landlord says his plumber fixed the fault on 14 May, but his only source is a text from the plumber (E018). The tenant's last report, on 13 May, was still no hot water (E017). Before the case can close, the tenant has to positively confirm the fix. Our voicemail (E019) and email (E020) on 15 May have had no reply. Loss of hot water was treated as urgent from the start (E004), so a short chase through a different channel (SMS) is justified, rather than waiting the usual 2–4 days. 16 May is a Friday, so the reply-by is the next working day. The letterbox issue was raised on 13 May and we promised to follow up (E017), but nothing has been done since. It costs nothing to pick it up in the same message and log it separately. The landlord asked to hear only if the problem continues (E018), so there is nothing to send him until the tenant replies.
decision.expectedOutcome: The tenant either confirms hot water and boiler power are working, which lets us tell the landlord and close the case, or reports the fault continues, in which case we tell the landlord the same day and use his offer to send the agency's contractor (E015). We should also get details to log the letterbox as a separate request.

This message makes no decision about charges for the call-out or the repair, and does not change what the tenant was told on 6 May.

No technical advice is given beyond stopping use and contacting us if anything seems unsafe.

If the fault continues: tell the landlord the same day and ask whether to send the agency's contractor now, as he offered on 12 May.
If there is no reply by 19 May: phone the tenant and consider escalating, given the length of the hot-water outage.
Log the letterbox as a separate request once details arrive, and ask the landlord how he wants to proceed.
The landlord's request for a building contact to message the tenant (E010) is still unresolved. The tenant's consent is needed before any of her details are shared.
